items.title: Calendar MCP Server
items.text:
Calendar MCP is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for iCalendar feed management and event queries. It lets MCP clients like Claude Desktop work with multiple calendar feeds for event tracking, conflict detection, and schedule management.

Use this documentation to:

  • Understand what the server does and how it is structured
  • Get started running it locally or via Docker
  • Configure environment variables and calendar feeds
  • See what kinds of tools and queries are available

For architectural details aimed at agents and contributors, see AGENTS.md in the repository root.

items.title: cache
items.text:
Cache layer for Calendar MCP services.

Cache is the facade the app uses. It serializes values as JSON, keeps hit/miss statistics, and never raises into the request path: backend errors are logged (rate limited), counted in CacheStats.errors, and turned into misses.

Backends: - PostgresBackend: a table in the service's own PostgreSQL database (DATABASE_URL). Connects lazily, backs off for 30 s after any database error, and creates its table on first use. - MemoryBackend: a process-local dict for local development and tests (CACHE_BACKEND=memory).

items.title: PostgresBackend
items.text:
PostgresBackend(conninfo: str, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic)

Cache table in PostgreSQL via a small sync connection pool.

Constructing it does no I/O. The pool opens on the first operation, the table is created once per process after the first successful connect, and any database error starts a 30 s backoff during which every operation is a miss and is_connected() is False (it never does I/O itself).

items.title: CacheTTL
items.text:
Standard TTL values for different data types.

All values can be overridden via environment variables by prefixing with CACHE_TTL_ For example: CACHE_TTL_CALENDAR_EVENTS=300 will set CALENDAR_EVENTS to 300 seconds

Environment Variables

CACHE_TTL_CALENDAR_EVENTS: Calendar events cache (default: 900 seconds) CACHE_TTL_CALENDAR_INFO: Calendar info cache (default: 1800 seconds)

items.title: glob_to_like
items.text:
glob_to_like(glob: str) -> str

Translate a cache-key glob into a SQL LIKE pattern (used with ESCAPE '\').

* matches any run of characters and ? any single character; every other character is literal, so %, _ and \ in the glob are escaped. Character classes ([abc]) are not supported and match literally.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: The Calendar MCP server is configured primarily via environment variables.

items.title: Core Settings
items.text:
• ICAL_FEED_CONFIGS (required) – JSON array of calendar feeds:
[
  {
    "name": "Work",
    "url": "https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/YOUR_ID/basic.ics"
  },
  {
    "name": "Personal",
    "url": "https://outlook.office365.com/owa/calendar/YOUR_ID/calendar.ics"
  }
]
  • TIMEZONE – IANA timezone name (default: UTC)
  • REFRESH_INTERVAL – Minutes between refreshes (default: 60)
  • DEBUG – Enable debug logging (true / false, default: false)

items.title: HTTP Mode
items.text:
Used by src/server_remote.py for remote access:

  • MCP_API_KEY – API key for authentication (strongly recommended)
  • MD5_SALT – Salt for MD5 hash (optional, recommended)
  • HOST – Bind address (default: 0.0.0.0)
  • PORT – Listen port (default: 80)

The HTTP MCP endpoint has the form:

https://your-domain.com/app/{API_KEY}/{API_KEY_HASH}/mcp

where API_KEY_HASH is calculated as:

  • MD5(MD5_SALT + API_KEY) when MD5_SALT is set, or
  • MD5(API_KEY) in legacy mode.

items.title: Cache (Optional)
items.text:
• DATABASE_URL – PostgreSQL URL for the response cache
  • CACHE_BACKEND – memory for a process-local cache (local development)

The cache is optional. CACHE_BACKEND=memory selects a process-local cache; otherwise a set DATABASE_URL selects PostgreSQL; with neither, every request parses the calendar feeds directly.

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host:5432/calendar_mcp?sslmode=require&application_name=calendar-mcp

The PostgreSQL backend:

  • connects lazily on first use (startup never waits for the database);
  • creates its table, cache_entries (an UNLOGGED table: a database crash may empty it), on first connect. The database user needs CREATE on schema public; if it lacks it, the server logs a warning naming the fix (GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO <user>, run as postgres);
  • never fails a request: after any database error it logs (at most once a minute per operation), serves misses and reads the calendar feeds directly for 30 seconds, then retries.

clear_cache takes a glob: * matches any run of characters and ? one character; character classes ([abc]) are not supported. get_cache_info reports the database host and name, never credentials.

items.title: Cache TTLs
items.text:
Override with CACHE_TTL_<NAME> (seconds):

Name Default Data CALENDAR_EVENTS 900 Event queries and search results (ical:events:*, ical:search:*) CALENDAR_INFO 1800 Calendar feed information (ical:info:*)

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: This guide shows how to run the Calendar MCP server and connect it to MCP clients.

items.title: Quick Start with Docker
items.text:
For production HTTP access:

cp .env.example .env.local
# Edit .env.local: set ICAL_FEED_CONFIGS and MCP_API_KEY

docker-compose up --build

After the container is running, you can calculate your MCP endpoint URLs:

python scripts/verify_auth.py --api-key YOUR_KEY --domain localhost:8080 --no-https

Key endpoints:

  • Health: http://localhost:8080/app/health
  • MCP: http://localhost:8080/app/{API_KEY}/{API_KEY_HASH}/mcp

items.title: Local Development (without Docker)
items.text:
1. Create a virtual environment:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
  1. Install dependencies:
pip install -e .
  1. Set environment variables (at minimum ICAL_FEED_CONFIGS):
export ICAL_FEED_CONFIGS='[{"name":"Work","url":"https://..."}]'
  1. Run the MCP server (stdio transport):
python src/server.py

For HTTP mode, use src/server_remote.py instead and configure MCP_API_KEY, HOST, and PORT.

items.title: MCP Tools
items.text:
The Calendar MCP server exposes a set of MCP tools for working with calendar data and cache management.

High-level categories include:

  • Calendar queries – Get events for today, upcoming events, and date/range-based queries
  • Service status – Inspect server and calendar service status
  • Configuration – View non-sensitive configuration values
  • Cache management – Inspect and manage the optional PostgreSQL (or in-memory) cache

Refer to:

  • src/server.py for server-level tools such as:
  • get_current_datetime
  • get_server_status
  • get_server_config
  • get_cache_stats
  • clear_cache
  • get_cache_info – returns connected, backend (postgres or memory), database (PostgreSQL host and database name, never credentials), server_version, entries and table_bytes
  • reset_cache_stats
  • src/services/ical.py for calendar-specific operations implemented by MultiCalendarService

For detailed design notes intended for AI agents and contributors, see AGENTS.md in the repository root.
